content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1, the no-cost rebalance. It lifts service level to 91.8% for 14:00–18:15, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"Two separate problems are running. First, the FD special-rate email (MKT-2026-556) is pushing general calls 20–45% over forecast, with new_offer_enquiry at 2.74x normal. Second, payments is about 4 agents short (35 vs 39) because of extra sick calls. Doing nothing (P0) is already predicted to reach 89.6% for the window. P1 does better at zero cost by briefly shoring up payments and then handing help back to general later. For 14:00–15:00 it moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments, delays payments breaks by 45 minutes and turns on IVR callback on payments. For 17:00–18:00 it moves 2 agents from payments back to general. Predicted results: payments 92.3%, general 91.4%, abandon rate 1.9% (vs 2.3% with no action), rest of day 92.7%. There are no policy issues.","trade_offs":["P2 is only marginally better (92.0% overall, 1.7% abandon) and targets the campaign callers directly with chat deflection, but it costs INR 528 for a 0.2-point gain.","P3 costs INR 540 in overtime yet scores lower (90.4%) and leaves general weakest of the options at 89.6%.","P1 takes 3 agents off general from 14:00 to 15:00 while campaign volume is still high, and it delays payments breaks by 45 minutes. General is still predicted at 91.4%."],"watch":"Watch general during 14:00–15:00 while the 3 agents are on payments, especially new_offer_enquiry volume from the campaign. If general falls noticeably, consider adding P2's chat deflection. Also check that the delayed payments breaks are taken and that the 17:00 move back to general happens."}
